references.text: The same warning about being cut off from one's people applies to anyone who makes the anointing oil for common use.
The expression 'cut off from their people' is also used regarding those who violate the Passover regulations.
The same penalty - being cut off from the people - applies to ritual impurity concerning holy things.
To be 'cut off from one's people' is the punishment for anyone who does not bring their offerings to the tabernacle.
The first time the expression 'cut off from their people' appears in the Torah is regarding the covenant of circumcision.
Anyone who sins deliberately shall be cut off from the people because they have despised the Lord's word.
Both verses illustrate the severe consequence of breaking God's holy laws: loss of membership in God's people.
The connection shows that copying sacred rituals for personal gain falls under the category of 'mocking the Lord with a high hand.'
Both verses emphasize that interfering with holy arrangements while unclean or without right leads to exclusion.
Both verses demonstrate the principle that desecrating what is holy (whether incense or sacrificial meat) results in being cut off.
